title: MV Issue with characters adjacent to star tiles

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I'm having issues where a star tile cuts off the top of the event just below it. I tried the CP_Large_Sprite_Fix plugin that's distributed in the dlc folder, but it doesn't seem to work properly (or I can't get it to work).
The plugin seems to be very poorly documented, so I could be doing something wrong. Alternatively, are there any other plugins that do a similar thing? I think I do recall seeing one that requires the star passability tile to have the DOWN direction set to block, but I don't remember what it was called or how I could search for it.
What I did:
Enable the plugin
Set terrain tag 7 on the specific star tiles that were cutting off tops (mainly the backs of chairs)
On one especially large event, I added the <large sprite> tag
What works:
Normal-sized (chibi) sprites are no longer cut off by a star tile placed above them. Thus, people sitting in chairs no longer have the top few pixels cut off.
What doesn't work:
Normal-sized sprites (including the player) are still cut off by star tile placed above them
when the tile they are on is also a star tile
.
The extra-large sprite is still cut off.
This image illustrates both issues:
Proof that those have terrain tag 7 set:
I've also attached a shot of the statue event, in case that's helpful (see below).
I am less worried about the large sprite, as I found I could work around it by setting it to display "above characters".

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Okay, I tried OcRam's. It work pretty well, but has a bit of a conflict with some of my other customizations. I think it did handle both of the cases in the original post. I don't remember if I tested it on extra-tall towers from Outside_C (by extra-tall I mean reduplicating those tiles to make a tower taller than 5 tiles). But then I realized that it's not free for commercial use, so I decided not to use it.
Thus, I'm now using Hudell's plugin. It works really well in general, but it's an extremely poor fit for those extra-tall towers – using the terrain tag to determine the height means that you need to duplicate the entire tower on your tilesheet with different tags. Since I only use the towers in a couple places, I just went ahead and did that, but… I think I wouldn't recommend Hudell's plugin for more complicated work. It's great for simpler stuff, although needing to set all the star tiles to terrain tag 1 (or occasionally more) was a bit of a pain.
I'll definitely give TF_LayeredMap a try later and see if it's a better fit for my next project, but for now I'm (barely) satisfied with Hudell's plugin.
Thanks for the help in finding these.

posts.author: emogal
posts.body:
What do you mean duplicate? You only need to have the tower on the sheet once, and then each tile it spans will have terrain tags equating to height. For example, the base of the tower (which I believe does not appear above the actor) would be marked as 0, then the next highest segment would be 1, and so on. If your tower is just the same "mid section" piece stacked multiple times, just use star tags for those pieces, since the player will never have occasion to be in front of them anyway...unless they can fly or something.
What I do in my game for tall trees is 0 for the roots, counter+1 for the trunk, counter+2 for the beginning of the leaves/branches that should hang over the player's head, and then everything else above that is a star tile without any counter or terrain tags. I believe the level of terrain tag is there to account for your character's sprite height and whether it exceeds the tile height to determine its appearance in front of or behind the counter+terrain tag tile.
As for not using cores, I've never understood why people have such arbitrary aversions to things set in place to help them. Some people on here refuse to use plugins at all, which seems absurd unless explicitly done to challenge oneself for fun. I'm certainly not going to sacrifice the potential of my project just because a great plugin requires a core to work.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
What you say is indeed true if there is in fact no way for the player to end up behind the tower. In a very simple setup, that might be a reasonable assumption. Perhaps there are only walls and roof behind the tower, and there's no way to climb up onto the roof.
But if you
can
climb up onto the roof, or if the tower is free-standing rather than part of a larger building, then that won't work. The tiles
absolutely must
have their height flag go up by 1 as y decreases, or it won't work.
I think it's likely your way also wouldn't work if you have an event whose sprite is larger than about 96x96, but I haven't tested, so I could be wrong.
My aversion to cores is not absolute. If the only plugin I could find required a core, and it was a big plugin that would be a pain to do myself, and I felt like I really needed that plugin, I would probably install the core and just use it. But having a core does apply a slight negative score for me when selecting between multiple similar plugins.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
So, just for the record, I found a bug in Hudell's plugin that causes it to
not
ignore the terrain height settings for non-star tiles.
The solution is to just add an extra pair of parentheses, replacing this:
JavaScript:
if (flag & 0x10 === 0)
with this:
JavaScript:
if ((flag & 0x10) === 0)
